stepNotes.1: The memory unit connects CLI, tool, route, and session adapters to scanning, curated mutation, prompt rendering, recall, diagnostics, evaluation, and two JSON-backed stores.
stepNotes.2: Curated rules and scope metadata cross user/model and filesystem boundaries; scanned repository text is also untrusted input when rendered into the system-prompt wrapper.
stepNotes.3: Recorder writes hold process and file locks and use atomic rename, but warmup loads before scanning and later saves outside those locks, allowing a concurrent curated entry to be lost.
stepNotes.4: The 32-path read cache and in-flight coalescing bound steady-state metadata, while persisted entry size and the pre-truncation directory listing remain workload-dependent.
stepNotes.5: Applicability and hashing have single policy owners; the missing domain-level warmup transaction forces CLI and server adapters to repeat an unsafe generate-then-save sequence.
stepNotes.6: The barrel example advertises nonexistent APIs, scanner failures can degrade without diagnostics, and abort-leak.test.ts is misplaced because it imports only src/util/abort.
stepNotes.7: Nine selected files passed 104 tests for filtering, diagnostics, ranking, mutation, corruption, caching, rendering, and CLI behavior, with no warmup-versus-record interleaving case.
stepNotes.8: The empty ledger contains no Critical item; the demonstrated lost-update sequence is a Medium candidate whose minimal fix is shared locking plus a deterministic race regression.
stepNotes.9: The exact focused Vitest selection and packages/ax-code typecheck passed, and no reviewed memory source file has a worktree delta.
